scopeNote: Rescoped from origin/codex/whitepaper-corpus-defrag (2026-08-31, commit 014d044d3 and follow-ups). That branch's corpus.json also relocated every whitepaper chapter and formal artifact into new co-located `formal/` trees and folded in a whitepaper chapter/collected-volume/research-publication/skill-satellite/atlas registry. wave-p1/proof-estate brings over only the piece it needs -- the formal-artifact and research-program manifest -- rewritten against the CURRENT (unmoved) file layout, with NO relocations. The chapter/mirror machinery is deliberately NOT carried over: whitepaper/textbook.json plus .github/workflows/library-checks.yml already are that registry's current, live source of truth on this branch (see the 'Textbook Edition' work); adding a second, divergent one here would just be a second place for it to drift. Policy: every on-disk formal artifact is WIRED (ci.status="wired", naming the CI job(s) that run it) or explicitly RETIRED (ci.status="retired", with a reason) -- no third state. See scripts/check-whitepaper-corpus.mjs.

forbiddenLegacyRoots.reason: The origin/codex/whitepaper-corpus-defrag branch this manifest was recovered from relocated every formal artifact into co-located `formal/` trees and treated analyses/, proofs/, docs/adr/models/, docs/harbor-research, docs/research, and docs/whitepaper-critical-review.md as forbidden legacy roots that must no longer exist. wave-p1/proof-estate deliberately did NOT perform that relocation (out of scope; the author reviews prose/structure moves separately), so every one of those roots still holds the estate's real, current files. Keeping this rule enabled would make the checker fail permanently against the actual current layout. Flip `enabled` to true only alongside an actual relocation PR that empties these paths.
